analysis.title: Energy Fuels Inc. (UUUU): Donald project receives conditional approval for up to A$180mn of Australian government financing; FID by year-end
key_insights: On 10/26, Export Finance Australia (EFA) and the National Reconstruction Fund Corporation (NRFC) conditionally approved up to A$180mn (US$126mn) of financing for Phase 1 of the Donald Rare Earth and Mineral Sands Project in Australia, as part of a proposed A$200mn senior project finance debt facility.
UUUU targets a final investment decision (FID) on Donald by year-end 2026. Donald is expected to be UUUU's first large-scale source of rare earth mineral feedstock.
Phase 1 is expected to produce ~9,000 tpa of rare earth element concentrate (REEC) over a 40-year mine life, plus ~225,000 tpa of heavy mineral concentrate.

Financing split: EFA up to A$70mn, NRFC up to A$110mn, and the remaining A$20mn from commercial lenders. The facility has a 10-year tenor from financial close, priced at BBSY plus a margin. Commitments remain subject to definitive documentation, due diligence, remaining debt funding and final approvals.

UUUU earns a 49% interest in the Donald JV (with Astron Limited) by funding the first A$183mn (US$127mn) of upfront equity. It has invested ~A$60mn (US$41mn) for a 15.3% stake and must invest a further ~A$86mn (US$60mn) plus issue US$14mn of common shares to reach 49%.
Phase 1 capex is estimated at A$450mn (US$317mn) per Astron. Astron has said FID was expected at the close of project financing negotiations, which GS cites as support for FID by year-end.

The ~9,000 tpa of REEC would be processed at the White Mesa Mill into ~1,000 tpa of NdPr oxide plus Tb and Dy oxides, feeding UUUU's metallization and alloying capacity acquired through ASM and, after the planned VAC acquisition, permanent magnet manufacturing.

Per the company, Donald's NdPr output could supply ~75% of the expanded ~3,600 tpa NdFeB alloy capacity at the Korean Metals Plant, and its REEC could support ~77% of VAC's existing magnet manufacturing capacity across US and European facilities.

GS is Not Rated on UUUU (price target and estimates removed) and discloses it is acting as financial advisor on an announced strategic matter involving Energy Fuels. Price was $7.56 at the 10/26 close, market cap $1.8bn, EV $2.0bn.

market_movers.rationale: Conditional A$180mn Australian government financing advances Donald Phase 1 toward a year-end 2026 FID. GS is Not Rated on UUUU, so this is a company-event update with no rating or target.

earnings_insights: GS forecast table (UUUU, Not Rated, GS estimates): revenue $65.9mn FY12/25, $146.1mn 12/26E, $207.5mn 12/27E, $280.8mn 12/28E. EBITDA -$95.7mn, -$52.0mn, -$5.9mn, $24.5mn. EPS -$0.38, -$0.22E, -$0.04E, -$0.02E.
Quarterly EPS: -$0.13 for 6/26 (reported), with estimates of -$0.02 for 9/26E, -$0.02 for 12/26E and -$0.01 for 3/27E.
risk_factors: The A$180mn commitments are conditional and subject to definitive documentation, due diligence, remaining debt funding and final approvals.
Discussions on the remaining commercial term loan and bank guarantee facilities are ongoing.
FID is targeted by year-end 2026 but not yet taken. UUUU must still fund ~A$86mn and issue US$14mn of shares to earn its 49% interest.
